downstairs.open_connection: living room is connected to kitchen by corridor, so thermostat represents a larger connected downstairs air volume

upstairs.note: Upstairs may settle at a different temperature than the downstairs thermostat because there is no separate upstairs sensor or zoning.

wood_heat.note: Wood stove operation is separate from the electric-boiler control decision; for electric tempering periods it is normally irrelevant because the stove is not being fed.

control_topology.note: The hydronic system is operated as one whole-house zone; room-by-room isolation is not used.
control_topology.distribution_note: One boiler call circulates heat through the whole hydronic system; model must not optimize rooms independently.

thermostat_context.location: ground floor near the wood stove, in the larger connected downstairs air zone
thermostat_context.model_role: single control temperature for the house
thermostat_context.note: The downstairs thermostat is the sole control reference. Wood heat can bias it only during stove-active periods; unattended electric tempering is evaluated separately.
thermostat_context.interpretation: The thermostat is a control point for the whole system, not a whole-house average temperature. Upstairs can remain cooler or warmer than the thermostat reading.
thermostat_context.tempering_relevance: During unattended electric tempering, wood-stove influence is absent; the main uncertainty is vertical temperature distribution between downstairs and upstairs.

dp2.note: OFF is frost-protection mode; MANUAL is manual temperature-control mode. DP2 is not relay/heat-demand state.

dp106.test_evidence: During manual heating-demand test, DP106 rose to 10; after setpoint was reduced below room temperature and heat demand should end, DP106 remained 10 for >10 minutes.
dp106.note: Do not use DP106 as ON/OFF heat demand. It may be a timer/counter or another auxiliary value.

heating_energy_model.note: This prior gives the absolute energy scale until winter observations can narrow it. Measured indoor/outdoor dynamics remain primary for timing and cooling behaviour.

control_principle.strategy: Use the full 6–8 °C band and thermal inertia instead of trying to hold exactly 7.0 °C.
control_principle.policy: The model can compare costs of alternative targets, but it must not change the configured 7 °C target automatically.

priority_order: protect the house and respect the configured tempering target
use the full thermostat hysteresis band and building thermal inertia
respect D45d/HDO boiler availability and prefer low-tariff operation
when several safe schedules have similar energy/cost, prefer the lower-carbon electricity window if reliable carbon-intensity data are available

tariff_control.rule: Use the current customer-specific ČEZ export as the schedule and check public ČEZ sources once daily for changes. Do not imply that the CAPTCHA-protected customer export itself is refreshed automatically.
tariff_control.source: current ČEZ DIP export supplied 2026-09-29 + daily public ČEZ schedule/change monitor
tariff_control.note: The current per-customer DIP endpoint is CAPTCHA-protected. The public-repo automation therefore keeps the current CEZ export authoritative and monitors public CEZ sources daily without paid providers.
tariff_control.heating_blocking_requirement: D45d requires technical blocking of electric heating during VT
tariff_control.control_rule: Treat HDO windows as intended boiler availability, but do not claim the physical HDO blocking wiring has been independently verified.

additional_nt_heating_blocking.model_policy: Treat published NT/VT timing as the normal tariff schedule, but do not assume electric heating is guaranteed available every NT minute. Avoid optimization that depends on a last-minute heating burst.

ecological_control.current_rule: Do not invent green hours. Until a reliable Czech-grid carbon-intensity source is connected, ecological optimization means minimizing kWh and avoiding unnecessary preheating.
ecological_control.future_rule: If exact HDO and trustworthy hourly grid-carbon data are both available, shift only discretionary preheating within the safe hysteresis band toward lower-carbon low-tariff windows.

constraints: whole-house hydronic loop only; no room-by-room optimization
thermostat near wood stove can be locally biased during wood heating
never preheat solely for price or carbon if forecast shows no thermal need
never lower the configured 7 C target automatically

sensor_model.current_policy: Use the downstairs EMOS temperature as the sole control and modelling reference. Upstairs temperature is not separately measured or controlled.
sensor_model.radiator_layout_role: Radiator distribution and room layout are contextual inputs for understanding heat distribution and losses, not separate control zones.
sensor_model.wood_stove_policy: Wood-stove-active periods may alter the downstairs temperature locally; electric-tempering analysis should distinguish those periods, but no second sensor is required.

thermostat_hysteresis_status.note: EMOS P56S11 officially supports DIFF 0.1–1.0 °C. The model uses DIFF 1.0 °C, but the setting is not currently read back from the cloud API.
